comments.author: TioEmir
comments.body_html:
the overwrite happened when you extracted the archives by hand with 7zip, before the Manager was involved. One of those mods ships its own copy of spt-core.dll, and extracting it over your install replaces the core with an older version, the game then refuses to start. The Manager couldn’t fix that, because by then the core was already replaced. But good news, the 0.4.2 (posted a bit ago) refuses to write over SPT’s core files during install, and tells you when a package contained them. So please do this:

  1. Keep your fresh SPT install
  2. Install 0.4.2
  3. Install your mods through the manager

If a mod ships core files you’ll see a message saying they were skipped, that tells us exactly which mod is the culprit, and the game should still start. If you hit it again after that, send me the message and I’ll dig in. 42 client mods is nothing unusual, and this isn’t a “too many mods” problem.

comments.author: TioEmir
comments.body_html:
Fixed in 0.4.3, which I just released. The lookup was requesting a trimmed set of fields from Forge that didn’t include each version’s download URL. As a result, the app could find your mods but had nothing to download, which is why it only reported the differences without downloading anything.

One thing worth noting: exports created before 0.4.2 don’t include each mod’s unique identifier, so restoring them falls back to matching by folder name. That works for most mods, but not all. Any mods that Forge can’t match that way ( or that aren’t available on Forge at all ) will still need to be installed manually, and the app will tell you which ones. If you export your mod list again using 0.4.3, future restores will use the mod identifiers for exact matching instead of relying on folder names.

Thanks for reporting this, and sorry for the inconvenience!!

comments.author: TioEmir
comments.body_html:
That polling loop just means the client never gets past the initial handshake, it doesn’t say why on its own. Two files would tell us:

1 - BepInEx/LogOutput.log ( in your SPT folder )

2 - The server console output from startup, from the first line

A few things worth checking meanwhile:

  • Do any mods show as incompatible with your SPT version in the Manager? 0.4.5 reads that from the mod itself and flags it in the list
  • Did you install anything that isn’t built for your SPT version? Mixing 4.0 and 4.1 mods is the most common cause of this!!
  • Does the game start if you disable all client mods? If yes, re-enable them in halves to narrow down which one it is

Also worth knowing: which Manager version did you install them with? 0.4.2 fixed a case where a mod package could overwrite SPT’s own core files, and 0.4.5 fixed disabling leaving a mod’s prepatcher running

Edit: One more thing worth checking… If the server console showed anything about your profile being invalid over an unrecognised item, don’t enable removeModItemsFromProfile, that deletes those items from your profile permanently. Update the mod that added them instead.
